app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

symptoms.potential_symptom: High upstream request latency in frontend-proxy when contacting image-provider
symptoms.evidence: Traces (30 total) show many frontend-proxy requests with ~10,000 ms latency that include calls to image-provider. Examples: traceID cab13d753c6eb4a391d92e1744db93da latency 10021.0 ms sequence 'frontend-web -> frontend-proxy -> image-provider'; traceID 983c71e06d1437945d471caea6b68a98 latency 10020.0 ms sequence 'frontend-web -> frontend-proxy -> image-provider -> frontend-proxy'; traceID e301f0b7e7cd0796d2f1d4f9145abdc1 latency 10001.34 ms sequence 'frontend-proxy -> image-provider -> frontend-proxy'. Traces contain no errors and pod/metric checks reported healthy, indicating the latency is likely caused by slow downstream calls rather than pod crash/restart.

symptoms.potential_symptom: Image-provider service responding very slowly (≈10s) causing downstream latency
symptoms.evidence: Multiple traces where image-provider appears show end-to-end latencies around 10,000 ms. Examples: traceID 558e7baa242edde0fd67117d0c39b716 latency 10019.0 ms sequence 'frontend-web -> frontend-proxy -> image-provider'; traceID bb774880df7a3e588618cbb9fcca352e latency 10001.163 ms sequence 'frontend-proxy -> image-provider'; traceID af9d2f5136da2d93cfd1bb181635613c latency 10000.652 ms sequence 'frontend-proxy -> image-provider -> frontend-proxy'. No error spans or anomalous pod metrics were reported, suggesting image-provider is slow to respond (possible processing/IO or external dependency delay) and is the root cause of the observed high latencies.

rca_tasks.investigation_goal: Confirm image-provider is the latency epicenter and identify internal cause (blocking external call, long processing, or worker exhaustion). Verify which pods handled the slow requests and search pod logs for long-running calls, timeouts or repeated slow external calls (~10s).

Two-sided connection check between frontend-proxy and image-provider: verify frontend-proxy configuration for the image-provider endpoint (host/port/URL/name used) AND verify image-provider Kubernetes Service/port/name match the frontend-proxy configuration to catch DNS/port/name mismatches or wrong port-name causing connection fallback or long waits.

Compare image-provider pod resource and latency metrics during incident window vs baseline to determine if CPU/GC/memory or resource saturation correlates with ~10s responses (rule out node/CPU-bound causes).

Inspect frontend-proxy (Envoy/client) timeout and retry configuration for upstream calls to image-provider to see if a 10s timeout, retry policy, or proxy-side queuing could explain observed 10s spans (verify settings in deployment/configmap and pod args/env).

Confirm trace-level span boundaries: retrieve traces filtered for high-latency calls involving image-provider to verify whether the ~10s is accounted for inside the image-provider span (service processing) vs waiting/retries in the proxy or network.

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: image-provider (astronomy-shop) is the latency epicenter due to internal worker/resource exhaustion in the image-provider pod: the NGINX-based image-provider is a single-replica pod (image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv) and its OpenTelemetry exporter is failing repeatedly with “OTel export failure: data refused due to high memory usage”, indicating memory pressure/telemetry exporter blockage that is exhausting workers and causing elevated latency. There is no evidence in the pod logs of long external/blocking calls (~10s) or timeouts.
rca_analyses_list.reasoning:
1) get_pods_from_service returned a single Running pod: image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv — all image requests go to this single replica (single point of contention).
2) get_logs from that pod shows continuous HTTP GETs served but repeated error lines: “OTel export failure: data refused due to high memory usage” at multiple timestamps. No log lines indicating long external request durations, external timeouts, or ~10s blocking calls. 
Together these show the service is overloaded internally (telemetry exporter memory pressure / exporter blocking) leading to worker/resource exhaustion and increased latency, rather than a slow external dependency or long internal processing per request.

task.investigation_goal: Confirm image-provider is the latency epicenter and identify internal cause (blocking external call, long processing, or worker exhaustion). Verify which pods handled the slow requests and search pod logs for long-running calls, timeouts or repeated slow external calls (~10s).

insights: Service image-provider in namespace astronomy-shop has a single Running pod: image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv (single-replica, single point of contention).

Pod logs show continuous successful image GET requests but repeated errors: "OTel export failure: data refused due to high memory usage" at multiple timestamps (evidence of OpenTelemetry exporter memory pressure).
No log evidence of long external calls, external timeouts, or ~10s blocking operations in the image-serving path—requests return 200 frequently, so per-request processing appears normal.

Repeated OTel export failures indicate telemetry exporter/backpressure causing memory pressure or worker exhaustion inside the NGINX-based image-provider, creating internal contention and elevated latency under load.

Root cause: internal resource exhaustion related to OpenTelemetry exporter (memory pressure/data refusal) on the single image-provider replica, producing latency issues — not a slow external dependency.

Checked logs for pod image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv using get_logs
Analyzed pod logs for error patterns and request traffic
Correlated pod list (single replica) with log errors to identify single-point contention
Formed and submitted final diagnosis via submit_final_diagnosis

load_module modules/ngx_otel_module.so;

pid /tmp/nginx.pid;

events {
    worker_connections 1024;
}

http {
    otel_exporter {
        endpoint otel-collector:4317;
    }
    otel_trace on;
    otel_trace_context propagate;
    otel_service_name image-provider;
    otel_span_name image-provider;


    include mime.types;
    sendfile on;
    server {
        listen 8081;
        listen [::]:8081;

        resolver 127.0.0.11;
        autoindex off;

        server_name _;
        server_tokens off;

        root /static;
        gzip_static on;

        location /status {
            stub_status on;
            access_log  on;
            allow all;
        }
    }
}

final_report.root_cause: The image-provider pod (image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv) exhausted internal resources due to OpenTelemetry exporter memory pressure and exporter failures ('OTel export failure: data refused due to high memory usage'). The exporter failures created backpressure / blocked exporter work paths inside the single-replica NGINX-based image-provider, exhausting workers and causing requests to queue or be delayed — producing the ~10s response latencies observed by frontend-proxy. The condition was amplified because the image-provider runs a single replica, making it a single point of contention for all image requests.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Traces: multiple traces (~30) show ~10,000 ms spans where image-provider is on the critical path (examples: traceIDs cab13d75..., 558e7baa..., bb774880...). 2) Pod listing: image-provider service backs a single running pod (image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-gnmjv). 3) Pod logs: repeated error lines from that pod stating 'OTel export failure: data refused due to high memory usage' at many timestamps. 4) No logs showing long external calls, timeouts, or external dependency delays (~10s). 5) Connectivity/config checks show frontend-proxy host/port (image-provider:8081) match the Service and Pod ports, ruling out DNS/port misconfiguration. Together these point to internal exporter-induced resource exhaustion on the single image-provider replica as the cause of elevated latency.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 investigation (completed): get_pods_from_service and get_logs on image-provider identified a single replica pod and repeated OpenTelemetry exporter failures in its logs; no evidence of long external calls. Diagnosis: internal worker/resource exhaustion in image-provider caused high latency. Priority-2 investigation (completed): verified frontend-proxy configuration and image-provider Service/Deployment ports and endpoints align (IMAGE_PROVIDER_HOST=image-provider, IMAGE_PROVIDER_PORT=8081; Service port tcp-service -> targetPort 8081; pod listens on 8081). No DNS/port mismatch found. Pending metric-level correlation and Envoy timeout/retry inspection were listed but not required to reach root cause because logs and traces provide a direct causal link. Conclusion: the exporter memory pressure and single-replica contention on image-provider are sufficient to explain the observed ~10s latencies.

- The priority reflects the likelihood that investigating that task/resource would uncover the root cause
